base_source: TTM through Q2 2026 from EDGAR 10-Q YTD (OCF $1,655.387M = FY25 $1,339.999M - H1'25 $572.425M + H1'26 $887.813M; minus SBC TTM $138.876M and capex TTM $2,146.311M = -$629.800M / 299.342M H1'26 diluted shares); normalized 3-yr median was -$2.41 and latest FY -$3.60 — all conservative bases negative, Tier F under every conservative base — see analysis.md
moat_justification: Moderate-strong: records storage has ~93-94% retention, ~14.5-year average storage duration, compliance/chain-of-custody switching costs, global scale (1,300+ facilities, 240,000+ customers) and proven pricing power, with cross-sell into Digital/ALM/data centres — but legacy volumes face secular digital substitution and growth leans on price, the data-centre moat is thinner against Digital Realty/Equinix/hyperscaler self-builds, most facility square footage is leased, and GAAP returns/book equity do not yet corroborate a wide moat through the build cycle.
name: Iron Mountain Incorporated
one_liner: Durable records franchise pivoting to data centres, moat 6/10 — but conservative owner's earnings are negative in 4 of the last 5 years (-$2.10/share TTM) because ~$2.1B/yr of growth capex exceeds operating cash flow on a $16.3B net-debt balance sheet, so it cannot clear the 15% hurdle at any price on an OE DCF; even charging only recurring capex gives just 7.7% weighted IRR (IV@15% $44 vs $115.10), so at $115 you pay 19.5x guided AFFO for a build wave, not for current owner's earnings.
sector: Real Estate / REIT — Records management & data centers
